title: Notice-driven SLA Degradation Playbook & PRD Acceptance Criteria for Burst Scenarios
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We need a clear, testable PRD that defines how hosted API SLOs should behave during notice-driven or unexpected burst traffic and the exact rollout gates for model or runtime changes. The goal is to ensure predictable application-level latency and availability while giving product teams the ability to roll forward safely. This ticket captures acceptance criteria, gating thresholds, rollback rules, and runbook links required for engineering and SRE to implement gated rollouts and automated pauses when error budgets or latency envelopes are violated.
background: Multiple teams have seen regressions after model swaps or runtime kernel changes during high burst traffic. Current rollout guards are generic; we need a formal notice-based degradation plan that ties to measurable error-budget burn rates, explicit canary windows, and fallbacks (quantized model variants or reduced-context mode). This PRD will be used by Release, Runtime, and Dedicated teams as the canonical gating spec.
scope_clarifications: Applies only to hosted API public endpoints (not private/VPC) unless the customer opts into Redwood-managed SLOs.
Per-tenant SLOs are out of scope for this ticket; separate initiative (PM-42109) will cover tenant-scoped SLAs.
This PRD covers both streaming chat and non-streaming generation routes, with slightly different metric definitions (time-to-first-token vs request tail latency).
Regional variance: EU regions should use same latency bands but tolerances for burst failover to a nearby region must be approved by Legal for data residency-sensitive customers (out of scope here).
acceptance_criteria: SLO definitions committed to docs: hosted-chat and hosted-generation SLOs published in Console SLO catalog.

Latency targets (measurement windows and labels):
- Hosted chat (streaming): TTF1 (time-to-first-token) median <120ms, p95 <320ms, p99 <700ms; streaming per-token latency p50 <20ms, p95 <60ms.
- Hosted generation (non-streaming): request latency p50 <180ms, p95 <420ms, p99 <900ms.

Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly for hosted API global control plane and model-serving tier; documented definition of 'availability' (successful 2xx generation start within 3x expected RTT) committed.
Error budget defined: monthly error budget = 0.05% of successful requests; convert to minutes and count for dashboards and automated gate checks.

Automated gate behavior implemented:
- Canary stage (1% traffic, 6 hours): abort/rollback if error-rate > 0.1% or latency p95 exceeds target by >25%.
- Progressive rollout (1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%): advance only if burn-rate <= 1 for previous window and no single-region outage.
- Immediate pause and automated fallback if rolling 1-hour burn-rate > 2 (i.e., consuming error budget twice as fast as baseline).

Fallback strategy described and implemented as runbook: automatically route to a compatible quantized model variant or reduced-context mode with documented quality degradation caveats and telemetry tags when SLO gates fail.

Observable dashboards and alerting: per-rollout dashboard with burn-rate, p95/p99 latency, error-rate, canary traffic percent, and a single 'gate health' boolean. Alerts wired for on-call when canary fails gate conditions.
Runbook & escalation: a clear on-call step-by-step (notify Release PM, SRE, Runtime Eng) and rollback procedure in Confluence with links included in ticket links below.
Acceptance test harness: synthetic traffic job that can replay representative burst patterns and validate gates in staging; jobs defined and scheduled in CI with pass/fail thresholds in PRD.
Docs and Console UX copy: short descriptions for rollout gates and what 'paused due to SLO' means for customers, staged into Console release notes.
Signoffs: PM (Aisha Patel), Runtime Eng lead (Marco Chen), SRE lead (Lena Kovács), and Legal for EU fallback wording (if applicable).
rollout_gates: Preflight: run synthetic traffic test suite (1000 QPS burst pattern) with golden metrics baseline; must be green before canary.
Canary: 1% traffic for 6 hours, must meet error and latency thresholds; automated rollback on any threshold breach.
Staged ramp: traffic increases only if burn-rate <= 1 for previous window and no single-region p99 spikes >2x expected.
Safety pause: if any window shows burn-rate >2 for 1 hour, rollout pauses and alert escalates to on-call; auto-fallback to quantized variant after 10 minutes if on-call does not acknowledge.
Final promotion: after 72 hours of stable metrics at 100% traffic and no sustained >5% error budget consumption, mark release as GA in release notes.
tradeoffs_and_open_questions: How aggressive should automatic fallback be for low-latency critical tenants? (Possible opt-in per enterprise customer later.)
Do we allow automatic cross-region failover for EU customers who require data residency? (Legal signoff required.)
Metric noise during bursts can make p99s volatile; should we use smoothed p99 windows for gate checks? Engineering prefers 5-minute rolling windows, SRE suggests 15-minute for stability.
Cost vs reliability: keeping extra reserved capacity improves pass rates but increases cost. Need to quantify expected additional cost for typical bursts and include in launch deck.
implementation_notes: Engineering to add gate-check hook in rollout controller that evaluates burn-rate and latency windows and exposes a 'canary_allowed' boolean via release API.
Telemetry: tag all canary requests with rollout_id and canary=true for filtering; ensure KV cache warmup runs prior to canary start window.
Staging harness: create a replay of three canonical burst patterns (sustained high QPS, sharp spike, prolonged medium spike) and verify differentiation in gates.
Rollback automation: implement a fast path to revert traffic split and engage quantized fallback variant in <2 minutes when triggered.
